article.title: Trump, Takaichi discuss Indo-Pacific security as Japanese leader reaffirms Taiwan policy
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original Mandarin article.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says she spoke to President Donald Trump on Thursday, discussing regional and international issues following Trump's meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Speaking to the press afterward, Takaichi said the two leaders also discussed the Indo-Pacific and the war in Ukraine during the roughly 20-minute call. “I will further elevate Japan’s relationship with the United States to a higher level,” Takaichi told reporters.

But Takaichi acknowledged differences with Washington over the International Criminal Court, which the U.S., China and Russia criticized in a joint declaration in Shenzhen. She said Japan has consistently supported the court and that Trump is aware of Japan’s position.
Earlier Thursday in Shenzhen, Takaichi told reporters there was “absolutely no change” in Japan’s position on Taiwan, as stated in the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique.
Takaichi added that Japan would continue close communication with Washington to strengthen the bilateral alliance and consult on a range of international issues.
VOA reached out to the White House for comment on the call but didn't receive a response at the time of publication.

Yu-Hua Chen, an associate professor in the Global Studies Program at Akita International University (AIU) in Japan, told VOA that U.S.-Japan relations under Takaichi have been particularly close. Tokyo has been using multiple institutional channels to maintain the relationship, with post-summit phone calls serving as one example.
Trump also spoke with Takaichi by phone after meeting Xi in Beijing in May.

Akita International University's Chen said Takaichi's latest remarks were considerably more moderate than her earlier comments in November 2025. This time, she returned to Japan's traditional approach of strategic ambiguity on Taiwan, he added.
"Takaichi's aim was probably to prevent tensions between Japan and China from escalating further," Chen said.

In November 2025, Takaichi told parliament that the use of military force by China on Taiwan, such as a naval blockade, would likely constitute a “survival-threatening situation” that would force Japan to respond.

Her remarks triggered strong protests from Beijing and contributed to a prolonged deterioration in bilateral relations. China subsequently increased pressure on Japan through measures including restrictions on exports to Tokyo, warnings against travel to Japan and tighter controls on strategic materials such as rare earths.

Takaichi's appearance at the APEC summit also underscored the difficult state of Japan-China relations. According to Japan's Kyodo News, Xi and Takaichi had a brief encounter at the summit's opening ceremony. Takaichi approached Xi, but he did not respond.

China also sent retired former ambassador to Greece, Zhang Qiyue, to receive Takaichi at the airport, rather than having a senior leader greet her. The reception contrasted with Xi's personal welcome for Trump and senior Communist Party official Cai Qi's reception of Putin.
Takaichi's visit had been viewed in Japan as an opportunity to restart high-level dialogue with Beijing. However, Xi did not hold any formal meetings with her.
Chen said the Japanese government had likely anticipated the relatively cool reception, but that Takaichi chose to attend the summit, nonetheless.

"This shows that Takaichi's approach to foreign policy is considerably more flexible than many observers expected," Chen said. "It also shows that Takaichi as prime minister can be very different from Takaichi as a member of parliament."

Takaichi has nevertheless reiterated her willingness to maintain communication with Beijing, saying before returning to Japan that she was not concerned that Trump's meetings with the Chinese and Russian leaders would undermine Japanese interests.
zh: 川普與高市紘子就印太安全議題進行討論，日本領導人同時重申對台政策
編者註：本文翻譯自原文（中文）。
日本首相高市早苗表示，她於週四與美國總統唐納德·川普通電話，在川普與中國國家主席習近平及俄羅斯總統弗拉基米爾·普京會晤後，雙方就區域及國際議題進行了討論。
會後接受媒體採訪時，高市表示，兩國領導人在這場約20分鐘的通話中，也討論了印太地區及烏克蘭戰爭等議題。「我將進一步提升日本與美國的關係至更高層次，」高市對記者表示。
不過，高市承認日本與華盛頓在國際刑事法院問題上存在分歧——美國、中國和俄羅斯曾在深圳發表的聯合聲明中批評該法院。她表示，日本一貫支持該法院，且川普也清楚日本的立場。
週四稍早，高市在深圳向記者表示，日本對台灣的立場「絕對沒有任何改變」，這與1972年《中日聯合公報》的表述一致。
高市還表示，日本將繼續與華盛頓保持密切溝通，以鞏固雙邊同盟關係，並就一系列國際議題進行磋商。
美國之音就這通電話一事向白宮尋求評論，但在發稿時尚未收到回覆。
日本秋田國際大學（AIU）全球研究學程副教授陳玉華向美國之音表示，在高市多美子任內，美日關係格外密切。東京方面一直透過多種制度性管道來維繫這段關係，峰會後的電話交談便是其中一例。
川普在五月於北京與習近平會晤後，也曾與高市通電話。
秋田國際大學的陳表示，高市最近的言論比她2025年11月的先前發言溫和許多。他補充道，這次她回歸了日本在台灣問題上一貫採取的「戰略模糊」方針。
「高市的目的，很可能是為了防止中日之間的緊張局勢進一步升級，」陳表示。
2025年11月，高市在國會表示，中國若對台灣動用軍事武力（例如實施海上封鎖），很可能構成「危及生存的局面」，迫使日本不得不作出回應。
她的言論引發北京方面的強烈抗議，並導致雙邊關係長期惡化。此後，中國透過多項措施對日本施加更大壓力，包括限制對日出口、發出赴日旅遊警告，以及加強對稀土等戰略物資的管控。
高市在亞太經合組織（APEC）峰會上的亮相，也凸顯了中日關係的艱難處境。據日本共同社報導，習近平與高市在峰會開幕式上曾有過短暫交會。高市主動走向習近平，但習近平並未回應。
中國還派出了已退休的前駐希臘大使張起月前往機場迎接高市，而非由高級領導人出面迎接。這種接待方式與習近平親自迎接川普，以及中共高層官員蔡奇迎接普京的情況形成鮮明對比。
在日本國內，一市女士的此行曾被視為重啟與北京方面高層對話的契機。然而，習近平並未與她舉行任何正式會晤。
陳表示，日本政府很可能已預料到會受到相對冷淡的接待，但高市仍決定出席此次峰會。
「這顯示，高市外政方針的靈活性遠超許多觀察家的預期，」陳表示。「這也顯示，身為首相的高市，與身為國會議員的高市，兩者之間可能大不相同。」
儘管如此，高市仍重申願意與北京方面保持溝通，並在返回日本前表示，她並不擔心川普與中俄兩國領導人的會晤會損害日本的利益。
